findings.reason: a section landing as a non-convergence measurement has no control at all, so nothing in §2 can show that its guard fires, and the node needs a control stated on the measure the section now delivers (the refusal record or the row replay).
findings.text: §2's clause (3) control reruns the fit and requires the reconstructed plasma current to leave the 1.5 % band "on every case", but the outcome paragraph added at plan.html:118 records that on none of the three stored cases did the class reach a fit, so there is no reconstructed plasma current on any case for the control to compare and the section's only negative control cannot be run

findings.reason: a coordinator composing the §4 node from the table would gate it on §2, which by the plan's own outcome delivered no fit, and dispatch the cost measurement against a section that cannot supply the case it times.
findings.text: the §0 contract table gives §3 and §4 "§2" under "Waits on", while plan.html:138 ("Waits on §8, whose nova-written ITER rows and two reconstructed states it scores") and plan.html:154 ("Waits on §8, the case on which the class has a fit to time") and the declared `plan-section-depends-on` all name §8

findings.reason: a reader who sizes or orders the work from the contract table never learns §9 exists, and the two stated effort figures disagree by exactly the section that was added.
findings.text: the §0 contract table still ends at §8, so the newly declared §9 (in `plan-section-declarations` and `plan-section-depends-on`) has no row, and the table's hours sum to 39 against the declared `plan-effort-hours` of 47

findings.reason: as written, a worker runs three cases whose stated failure mode is exactly the solve its iteration performs, and clause (2) will record non-convergence for every case with no reading available to say whether the estimator or the forward solve failed.
findings.text: §9's stated root cause is that the nested class fails because the forward solve it needs near the stored states does not converge ("stalls at a residual of 1.2e-4", "TCV stalls at 0.03", "the ITER state resolves no magnetic axis"), yet its remedy is a pass loop that every iteration updates the flux map from the plasma current the fit implies, which is itself a free-boundary solve at a state chosen by the data rather than by a proposal; the section nowhere states why that solve converges where the cited solves did not, so the endpoint that clause (2) asserts against these three cases rests on the very mechanism its evidence reports as refusing

findings.reason: a worker following the section as written submits three jobs for one receipt, which the lead's one-measurement-one-job rule forbids, so the section's evidence clause has to name one allocation that runs the cases in sequence or as a few workers in it.
findings.text: §9 fixes its evidence as "one batch job per machine on the H200", that is one scheduler job per case for a single receipt, while the repository's binding measurement rule requires one measurement over many rows to be one job that shards its rows inside the allocation

findings.reason: the clause swaps a stored-case wall that existed for a synthetic-case wall that does not, and the node has either to measure imas-efit's wall itself (a deliverable the section does not declare) or to lose the comparison it was added for.
findings.text: §4's clause (3) asks for "imas-efit's recorded per-slice wall for the same case", but the same case is now the §8 ITER case, a run that §8 creates for the first time from nova-written rows and whose own done-when records no imas-efit timing, so no recorded per-slice wall exists for it to quote

findings.reason: the citation is misdirected rather than wrong in substance — the cost measurement exists in the plan, at §4 — so only a sentence moves and no node's endpoint changes.
findings.text: §9 asserts "§2 measured what that costs on real machines", but §2's done-when (plan.html:119-134) reports no wall, cost or forward-solve count, and the plan gives cost to §4
